I just ran a type‑check on the whole project with `bunx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | head -30`. The command completed, and the tool returned the first thirty lines of compiler output. Scanning those lines, I can see a few type errors that I’ve already addressed (the race condition fix, the removal of the stale `useEffect` that updated the tool hint, etc.). However, the output stopped at line 30 and the compiler was still reporting additional errors beyond that point – the tail end of the list was cut off. 

Since the next steps depend on fixing all type errors, I need to see the rest of the messages. The simplest way is to re‑run the same type‑check but capture more lines of output. Using `head -40` will give me ten more lines, which should be enough to see the remaining errors and decide whether they’re new issues introduced by the recent edits or leftover problems that need further fixes.

I don’t need to change directories because the tool runs in the repository root by default, and `bunx` will resolve the local TypeScript installation. I’ll also keep the redirection `2>&1` so that both stdout and stderr are captured, then pipe through `head -40` to limit the output size for readability.

Thus the next action is to invoke a Bash tool call with the extended command and an appropriate description.
